reviewer: Codex separate implementation and evidence review
scope: Additional unscored selection questions and automatic eligibility; no scored bank or assessment edits.

findings.review: Identity-conscious preferences are assessed separately from efforts to develop skills or remove opportunity barriers. Neither policy is inferred from Culture–Nature, Progressive–Traditionalist or another existing axis.

All subjects use the same two affirmative prerequisites; no politician-specific exception. Opposing, neutral and missing responses cannot qualify. The access statement does not block eligibility. Both comparison directions use the same rule.

Harris opposed SFFA in her own published statement. Mapping that position to Disagree on selection-admissions is inferred, not an exact questionnaire response. Her statement does not establish a hiring quota or rejection of achievement. Those positions are not fabricated.

This tests the catalogue Meritocracy template. Meritocracy and DEI have contested, varied meanings. Other profiles lack supplemental evidence and cannot qualify until researched. No claim of empirical instrument calibration or universal definition.
All 240 existing answers and scores are retained; supplementary evidence is separate. Legacy saved results remain readable and missing selection evidence does not establish eligibility.
